Norway's recent increase in its wealth tax, intended to generate an additional $146 million in annual revenue, resulted in a net loss of $448 million due to capital flight. The tax hike, which raised the maximum nominal rate to 1.1% and increased dividend taxes by approximately 20%, prompted an exodus of wealthy individuals and business owners, with an estimated $54 billion in wealth leaving the country. This departure led to a loss of $594 million in potential wealth tax revenue, significantly undermining the policy's intended fiscal outcome. The phenomenon has been described as an unprecedented capital flight, with many high-net-worth Norwegians relocating to more tax-friendly jurisdictions such as Switzerland. The situation has sparked debate over the effectiveness of wealth taxation in a globalized economy, with critics arguing that such policies can drive away capital and entrepreneurs, ultimately reducing the tax base.
